---
title: "Methods, assumptions, and status"
---

## The scientific question

Which observed predictors are associated with several continuous outcomes, after
accounting for dependence left in the responses? DrFARM was developed for
pleiotropic-variant analysis in multi-trait GWAS. Its design matrix can also hold
non-genetic predictors; this does not change the supported continuous-response
model into a generalized-response model.

The working representation is

$$Y=X\Theta^T+ZB^T+E.$$

Each row is one participant. `X` is n by p and `Y` is n by q. The fitted
coefficient matrix `Theta` is **q by p**: outcome rows, predictor columns.
`B` is q by k. Sparse-group penalties act on entries and predictor columns of
`Theta`; the factors represent the latent response component. They do not impose
a low-rank factorization of `Theta`. Association alone is not a causal effect.

## Choose the appropriate path

| Path | API | What its diagnostics establish | Inference status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Historical DrFARM | `DrFARM.one()` or `DrFARM.whole()`, default `coefficient.update = "historical"` | Historical loss-change rule plus the native inner coefficient-change rule | Original formulas remain available; maintenance tests do not establish new calibration claims |
| Weighted coefficient option | Same DrFARM calls with `coefficient.update = "weighted"`; standalone `remMap.weighted()` | The inner solver checks its weighted sparse-group objective's KKT residual; the outer procedure remains the preserved DrFARM composition | Explicitly `unvalidated_for_weighted_update` |
| Gaussian ECM reference | `gaussian.ecm.reference()` | Fresh observed Gaussian objective and stationarity diagnostics at the returned tuple | `not_provided`; no debiased estimate, standard error, or p-value |

The weighted option and ECM reference are development features introduced after
the public 0.1.0 source. Install the documentation's matching candidate before
using them. The function reference gives each argument and return value.

## Scale and output interpretation

By default, DrFARM fitting and precision estimation center every column and
divide by its sample standard deviation. `Theta` then maps standardized
predictors to standardized outcomes. The package returns no intercept or
automatic back-transformation. Use consistent preprocessing for initialization,
precision, fitting, and inference; `standardize = FALSE` means the caller owns
the working scale. Constant columns cannot be standardized.

The standalone weighted solver and Gaussian ECM reference use the supplied scale
with no automatic standardization or intercept. Their losses are summed, not
divided by n. Their C mask fixes C=0 entries to zero, penalizes C=1 entries with
both penalties, and leaves C=2 entries outside both penalties and the group norm.

For `K = NULL`, `X %*% t(Theta)` is the observed-predictor component on the working
scale. `E.Z %*% t(B)` describes the training latent component. Factor scores use
the observed outcomes and are not automatically known for a new participant.
There is currently no general `predict()` method. Factor coordinates can rotate;
compare their fitted products and implied covariance rather than arbitrary signs.

## What the penalty selects

For the default all-penalized coefficient matrix,

$$\mathcal P(\Theta)=\underbrace{\lambda_1\sum_{r,j}|\Theta_{rj}|}_{\text{individual associations}}+\underbrace{\lambda_2\sum_j\|\Theta_{\cdot j}\|_2}_{\text{whole predictors}}.$$

The entry penalty can remove individual predictor–outcome associations; the group
penalty can remove an entire predictor column. This describes a penalty, not an
inference test. The weighted solver reference documents the C mask and the summed
loss normalization.

## Why the Gaussian reference is separate

The reference assumes independent rows,
$z_i\sim N_k(0,I_k)$, diagonal positive residual covariance
$\Psi=\operatorname{diag}(\psi)$, and independence of factors, errors and observed
predictors. Under this explicit Gaussian model, the factor-conditional and
integrated observed-predictor mean coefficient is the same `Theta`.

With $R=Y-X\Theta^T$ and $\Sigma=BB^T+\Psi$, its target is

$$L=\frac n2\log|\Sigma|+
\frac12\operatorname{tr}(R\Sigma^{-1}R^T)+\mathcal P_C(\Theta),$$

omitting the constant $nq\log(2\pi)/2$. Each cycle freezes one posterior of the
factors, updates the sparse coefficients, and uses that same coefficient matrix
in the loading and full expected-residual-variance updates. It then recomputes
the observed objective and gradients. An unsuccessful trial returns the last
accepted tuple. A positive `psi.min` is an explicit variance constraint; zero
does not enable an automatic floor.

This procedure omits DrFARM's inner debiasing and **changes the estimator**.
The original outer monitor, inner debiasing, and covariance updates are retained
in both DrFARM paths. Their full composition is not certified as an optimizer of
this Gaussian objective. A successful weighted coefficient solve alone does not
establish that certification.

Successful reference stopping requires the configured first-order stationarity tolerance and a small
relative observed-objective change, or a starting tuple already within that stationarity tolerance.
These checks establish neither global optimality nor inferential validity. A
zero-loading start can be a stationary saddle.

## Recorded examples and limits

The retained 0.1.0.9002 execution on R 4.3.3 / Ubuntu 24.04 used fixed small
fixtures, then one common-start bundled-data comparison. These are optimization
diagnostics, not a simulation study of estimation accuracy or inference.

| Recorded reference case | Result |
|---|---|
| Two analytically stationary small starts | Returned unchanged, `initial_stationary`, zero cycles |
| Asymmetric n=4, p=1, q=2, k=1 fixture | `stationarity_and_objective` after 65 cycles; objective 6.4081872518; maximum score/n 9.53725e-7 |
| Four n=500, p=10, q=5, k=2 bundled-data grid cells | All reached `max_iter = 500`; all remained above the 1e-6 score tolerance |

The four reference grid objectives were lower than the corresponding preserved
fits, but none of those four cells converged. They are not rerun to render this
site. The small asymmetric example is distributed as
`inst/examples/gaussian-ecm-reference.R`. Recreate and compare the small fixtures
from a source checkout using new output directories:

```sh
Rscript --vanilla tools/reconcile-outer.R --output outer-small
Rscript --vanilla tools/compare-gaussian-ecm.R \
  --fixtures outer-small/fixtures.rds --output ecm-small
```

The bundled 500-cycle results above are retained evidence rather than a site
build dependency. Retain each reproduction's source, input, environment and
stopping records.

## Inference and unresolved behavior

`entry.pvalue()` retains historical outer-debiasing inference. It requires a
compatible predictor precision estimate, positive residual variance and positive
residual degrees of freedom. Neither the weighted update nor the ECM reference
adds inferential validation.

`pleio.pvalue()` preserves the two-sided Cauchy-tail formula
`2 * pcauchy(-abs(mean(1 / tan(pi * p))))` for each predictor. It differs from the
usual one-sided Cauchy combination; its intended test and boundary behavior
remain unresolved. Do not substitute a new tail silently.

The optional-K paths have a demonstrated whole-grid scoring basis mismatch;
the introductory examples use `K = NULL`. The reference itself supports only
independent rows. Generalized-response DrFARM, new response families, and Python
support are not established by this work.

The package is implemented in R with an existing Rcpp kernel. Read the
[Gaussian ECM derivation](../../docs/GAUSSIAN_ECM_REFERENCE.md),
[weighted objective](../../docs/WEIGHTED_UPDATE.md), and
[known issues](../../docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md) for details. The
[recorded ECM summary](../../pkgdown/assets/evidence/gaussian-ecm-summary.json) binds these numbers
to the previous source and execution; the site build does not rerun that grid.

*Latent factors. Explicit assumptions.*
